info.title: Insyte API
info.description:
## Versions

Every answer carries `Insyte-Version`, the dated version it is in: the one the call names in an `Insyte-Version` header (2026-10-01, 2026-07-01, 2026-04-01), or else the key's own, the newest on or before the day it was made. A version there is none of is refused with `InvalidRequestV1` (`field: insyte-version`).

## Webhooks

Endpoints are added in Instellingen → Webhooks. Insyte POSTs one JSON envelope per event: `{ id, type, api_version, created_at, workspace_id, store_id, data }`, `data` being the record in the endpoint's API version. A test send has `"test": true` and an empty `data`.

Headers: `Insyte-Event` (the type), `Insyte-Delivery` (this delivery), `Insyte-Api-Version`, and `Insyte-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is `hex(hmac_sha256(secret, t + "." + raw_body))`. During a secret rotation two `v1` values are sent for 24 hours; accept either. Refuse a `t` older than 300 seconds (replays), and compare in constant time.

Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else, a redirect or a time-out is a failure and is tried again on the endpoint's policy (1 m, 10 m, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 72 h). After 5 failed attempts in a row Insyte switches the endpoint off. Order is not guaranteed and an event may arrive twice: order by `created_at`, dedupe on `id`.

Before each attempt Insyte resolves the endpoint's name and refuses one that points at a private or internal address. That check is defence in depth, not a guarantee against a name that answers differently a moment later (DNS rebinding): authenticate every request by its signature, never by where it came from.

| Group | Events (✓ sent today) |
| --- | --- |
| orders | `order.created` ✓, `order.paid`, `order.fulfilled` ✓, `order.delivered`, `order.refunded`, `order.cancelled` ✓, `order.delayed` ✓ |
| refunds | `refund.created`, `refund.failed` |
| customers | `customer.created` ✓, `customer.updated` ✓, `customer.merged`, `customer.blocked` |
| products | `product.created`, `product.updated` ✓, `product.archived` ✓ |
| inventory | `inventory.low`, `inventory.out` |
| support | `ticket.created`, `ticket.replied`, `ticket.assigned` ✓, `ticket.closed` |
| chargebacks | `chargeback.opened`, `chargeback.evidence_due`, `chargeback.won`, `chargeback.lost` |
| suppliers | `supplier.delay_reported`, `supplier.message`, `supplier.order_accepted` |
| automations | `automation.run.completed`, `automation.run.failed`, `automation.published` |
| affiliates | `affiliate.applied`, `affiliate.approved`, `affiliate.payout.approved` |

get.description: The key making the call: its scopes and the workspace it belongs to.
The workspace's members. Needs `team.read`.
The workspace's roles and what each may do per area. Needs `team.read`.
The workspace's orders as Shopify holds them, newest first: `q` searches number and customer, `status` one status, `cursor` the next page. Needs `orders.read`.
The workspace's products by title, with their price range and stock. Needs `products.read`.

The products running low: a variant at or under `threshold` units over every location (the workspace's default, 12, if not given), sold out first, then the soonest to run out at the last 30 days' pace. Archived products are left out. Read only. Needs `products.read`.
The workspace's customers by name. Needs `customers.read`.
Where an order's parcels are: carrier, tracking number, status, the latest checkpoint, an exception, and when it was delivered; whether the order is delayed. Needs `orders.read`.
One order with its lines, address, internal note and refunds. Needs `orders.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Adds and removes the order's tags; Shopify hears it a few seconds later. Insyte's own markers (`at_risk`, `tracking_sent`, `draft`) are refused. Needs `orders.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: The team's internal note on the order; empty clears it. Never sent to Shopify or a supplier. Needs `orders.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

patch.description: The order's shipping address (the name and phone stay); Shopify hears it a few seconds later. `country` is ISO 3166 alpha-2. Needs `orders.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Cancels the order in Insyte and Shopify, without a refund. Irreversible: send an `Idempotency-Key`. Refused for an order already closed or with parcels on their way. Needs `orders.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Marks the order delayed (Insyte's `at_risk` marker): it shows as delayed and the `order.delayed` event follows a few seconds later, for automations and webhooks. The shopper is not mailed. Refused for an order closed or delivered; an order already delayed stays as it is. Needs `orders.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

delete.description: Takes the delay off the order. Insyte does not raise it again until something new happens: the carrier reports the parcel again and it then stands still or goes wrong, or the supplier misses a later hand-off. A delay marked by hand and cleared within its few seconds sends no `order.delayed`. Needs `orders.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Mails the order's shopper in the store's name, with these words (paragraphs split on blank lines). It goes a few seconds later, from the brand's own domain where one is verified; an answer goes to the store's reply address or its support mailbox. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: the same key sends once. `409 no_email` when the order has no address. An agent's key mails over MCP, where it is refused for now. Needs `support.write` and `orders.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Refunds part or all of what is left on the order, through its original payments. Irreversible: send an `Idempotency-Key`, which also makes Shopify refund once. Needs `orders.write` and `refunds.write`, within the key's limit; `pending` until Shopify took it.

get.description: The workspace's suppliers and how each takes its orders. Needs `suppliers.read`.

A supplier's monthly statements, newest first: the lines it shipped at their cost price less its returns refunded, and whether each is paid; the running month first while it has lines. Needs `suppliers.read`.
The forwarding queue: every open leg, or one view of it (`to_forward`, `awaiting`, `forward_error`), oldest first, with the counts. Needs `orders.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Forwards legs to their suppliers. They wait a few seconds, then go by the supplier's API or mail; a supplier gets only its own lines and the address, never the customer's email or phone. Legs without a supplier or with a paused one are refused (`409`). Needs `orders.write`.

note.description: For the suppliers; never the internal note.

via.description: How a supplier gets them, by supplier id, where it should differ from its own setting.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Moves a leg not yet sent to another supplier that is not paused; it is to be forwarded again, there. Needs `orders.write`.

get.description: Returns and claims, newest first, up to 500, or those in one status; with the queue's counts. Needs `returns.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Starts a return for a shopper; it waits for review. A claim reason makes it a claim. Lines already in a return, or whose product rule allows no return, are refused (`422`). Needs `returns.write`.

reason_id.description: One of the workspace's reasons: too_small, damaged, …

get.description: One return with its lines, its window and the resolutions it allows with what each moves. Needs `returns.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Approves a return in review. Needs `returns.write` and `returns.approve`.

keep_item.description: A claim settled without sending anything back.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Rejects a return, with the reason. Needs `returns.write` and `returns.approve`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Asks for a return label from the carrier the return address names; it is made a few seconds later (`label.state`). Refused (`409`) where no carrier is set up (`labels_unavailable`) or a label cannot be made (`no_return_address`, `no_shopper_address`). Needs `returns.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: The shopper sent the parcel themselves ("zelf versturen"): its carrier and tracking number, followed like a label's. Needs `returns.write`.

tracking.description: The tracking number the shopper sent the parcel with.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Marks the parcel received. Needs `returns.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Records the inspection; the return is then ready to settle. Needs `returns.write`.

lines.description: Per line; without, every line is in order and goes back on the shelf.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Settles a return that is ready, with a resolution it allows, at the amount the rules give. A refund goes back through the order's payments and is irreversible: send an `Idempotency-Key`, which also makes Shopify refund once. Needs `returns.write`, and `refunds.write` within the key's limit for a refund.

get.description: Tickets in the board's order, up to 500: by default every one, or one view (all is the board, open is not done and not set aside); with each view's count. Needs `support.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Writes a ticket by hand, at the top of the board; its assignees hear of it. About one order or one customer at most. Needs `support.write`.

get.description: One ticket with its comments. Needs `support.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

patch.description: Changes a ticket's title, description, priority, deadline or labels. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Moves a ticket to another column; done records when. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Puts a teammate on the ticket; they hear of it. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Takes a teammate off the ticket. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Adds a comment to the ticket's activity, as the key. Needs `support.write`.

mentions.description: Member ids the comment names; each hears of it.

live_version.description: The published version that runs; 0 for a draft.

trigger.description: The draft's trigger step, if it has one.

get.description: The workspace's flows, newest first, with each status's count. Needs `automations.read`.

live_version.description: The published version that runs; 0 for a draft.

trigger.description: The draft's trigger step, if it has one.

branches.description: A yes/no split's two lanes, which merge back into the line after it.
A yes/no split's two lanes, which merge back into the line after it.

severity.description: error stops publishing; warning does not.

get.description: One flow: its draft and live steps, its published versions, and what is wrong with the draft per step. Needs `automations.read`.

status.description: running, waiting, succeeded, failed, stopped or skipped.

reason.description: Why it failed, stopped or was skipped.

manual.description: Started by hand (again, or through this API).

status.description: ok, error, skipped, waiting, pending or stopped.

steps.description: Each step of the run's version and what it did; empty in a list.

get.description: The flow's runs, newest first, in pages of up to 200. Needs `automations.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

status.description: running, waiting, succeeded, failed, stopped or skipped.

reason.description: Why it failed, stopped or was skipped.

manual.description: Started by hand (again, or through this API).

status.description: ok, error, skipped, waiting, pending or stopped.

steps.description: Each step of the run's version and what it did; empty in a list.

post.description: Runs the flow's live version for one order now, as its trigger would, and answers the run as it started; its steps act as the flow's own service account. Refused for a flow never published (`409`, `not_published`); a paused flow's run is written `skipped`. Needs `automations.write`.

schema.description: A calendar month, YYYY-MM.
A calendar month, YYYY-MM.

get.description: Analyse: month `a` against month `b`, both cut to the shorter one's days (a month under way runs to today), in six figures: counted revenue (minor units, each day at its exchange rate), paid orders, on time (% of orders delivered, by the day delivered), refunded (% of orders placed with a refund since), disputes (cases opened, by the day opened) and hours to done (tickets by the day they came in). Inside the key's stores. Needs `analytics.read`.

schema.description: Comma-separated figures, as INSYTE() names them: omzet, bestellingen, gemiddelde_bestelling, terugbetaald, chargebacks, advertentiekosten, overige_kosten, kosten, nettowinst, marge, roas, advertenties_meta, advertenties_google (omzet_meta, omzet_google, omzet_klaviyo and omzet_organisch are not kept yet).
Comma-separated months, YYYY-MM, up to 24; the month under way when left out.

get.description: The figures a sheet's INSYTE() reads, each over a whole calendar month (the month under way to today), inside the key's stores and in the workspace's currency: sales from the counted orders, what was put under dispute that month, and Kosten's costs, net profit, margin, ROAS and ad spend per platform. One answer per metric and month, metrics first. Needs `analytics.read`.
Rekenbladen: the sheets of the member who made the key (their own and those shared with them), newest change first, archived ones included. Needs `data.read`.
One sheet with every tab as typed (cells, formats, column widths). Needs `data.read`; a sheet the key's member cannot open is not found.
Kennisbank: the published chapters, by title. A draft, a change not yet published and an archived chapter are never here. Needs `support.read`.
One published chapter with its published text. A chapter never published, archived, or for a store the key does not reach is not found. Needs `support.read`.
Klantagent: whether the customer agent is on, each channel's mode as set and as it works now, its hours, when it hands over and its tone. Changed in the console only. Needs `support.read`.
The customer agent's day so far, in the workspace's time zone, within the key's stores. Needs `support.read`.

What needs the team on Start, ranked by how soon: a delayed order, a return waiting for review, a quality check sent in, a sold-out variant, a store without its link. `needs_you` (the default) is what is red or amber; `all` adds the rest and what was seen in the last day. The rows narrow to what the key's scopes may read.

One plate Insyte drew for a queue row: what it found, the record as it stands and as drawn, how sure the rule is and why, and what filing runs. Readable with the scope of its record (`returns.read`, `products.read`).

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Files a plate: the command it carries runs as this key, with the scopes that command needs (approving a return takes `returns.write` and `returns.approve`; the delay mail `orders.write`; a reorder ticket `support.write`). A plate no longer open, or whose record moved on, is refused (`409`, `closed` or `stale`); one whose command did not go (`execution_failed`) is tried again.

get.description: Chargebacks, nearest deadline first, up to 500: action_required (open or waiting for evidence), submitted, won or lost; with each tab's count and the workspace's record. Needs `chargebacks.read`.
One chargeback with its evidence pack and its timeline. Needs `chargebacks.read`.
The programme's affiliates, with their codes, tiers, conversions and commission to date. Needs `affiliates.read`; a key held to some stores reads no money (only a key over every store does).
One month's payouts (the last ended month by default): per affiliate what is past its return window, what is still in it, reversals and the status. Nothing moves money here. Needs `affiliates.read`.

schema.description: A calendar month, YYYY-MM, in store time.
A calendar month, YYYY-MM, in store time.

get.description: Kosten: every cost line with what it costs in each month of the range (by default the five months up to the current one, at most 36), and each month's figures from revenue to net profit. Revenue is the counted orders' in the key's stores. Needs `analytics.read`.

schema.description: Comma-separated months, YYYY-MM, up to 36.

get.description: The month figures alone: revenue, orders, ad spend, other costs, net profit, margin and ROAS. Needs `analytics.read`.

Sync health: every store in the key's stores with its connection's state, its open incidents and the week's resolved ones, each with what Insyte already tried. Checked every 15 minutes. Needs `data.read`.
Data: the workspace's CSV imports not removed, newest first, at most 200. Needs `data.read`.
Data: the exports the workspace's members asked for, newest first, at most 100. The file itself downloads only in the console, for the member who asked. Needs `data.read`.
One export and how far it is. Needs `data.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Asks Vraag Insyte a question about the workspace and answers when it has settled. It reads only what this key's scopes and stores may (orders, tickets, chargebacks, the queue, Analyse and the month figures), counts against the workspace's AI budget, and changes nothing. A spent budget or a model that did not answer settles the answer as `failed`. An agent's key asks over MCP (`ask_insyte`). Needs no scope of its own; each read needs the scope it would on its own.

thread_id.description: A conversation of this key's to ask on; absent, a new one, titled by the question.

get.description: This key's conversations with Vraag Insyte, the latest first, up to 50. Needs no scope: they are the key's own.
One of this key's conversations, every question and answer in order. Needs no scope: it is the key's own. An answer that read a store the key no longer reaches is withheld.

schema.description: all is the inbox (not archived, spam, in the trash or snoozed); unassigned and linked (to a ticket) within it; archive, spam and trash.
A mailbox's id, or a chat channel's.
One store's chats; mail is no store's.
The subject, who is on it, and what it says.
1–200, 50 by default.

get.description: The inbox's mail threads and website chats, newest first, a page at a time, with how many match. Every mail, and the chats of the key's stores. Needs `support.read`.
One thread with its messages, or a chat with its messages and handover. Needs `support.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Replies to who wrote last, from the mailbox it came in at (mail), or in the shopper's widget (a chat). It waits out a few seconds first. A chat someone took over, or one that closed, is `ConflictV1` (`taken_over`, `closed`). Needs `support.write`.

body.description: Plain text; the mailbox's signature is added.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Puts one teammate on the thread. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Takes the teammate off the thread. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Moves the thread out of the inbox into the archive. Needs `support.write`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Gives a website chat to a teammate, as their "Overnemen": Insyte's customer agent stays silent on it, and only they reply. An agent's key cannot. Needs `support.write`.

member_id.description: The active member who takes the chat over.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Gives a website chat back to Insyte's customer agent ("Teruggeven aan Insyte"). Needs `support.write`.

get.description: The team's chat channels and the channels shared with suppliers. People's direct messages are theirs: a key reads none. Needs `support.read`.

schema.description: A message id: the messages before it.
1–100, 50 by default.

data.description: Oldest first: the newest page, or the one before `before`.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `before` for the older messages.

get.description: A chat's messages, 50 at a time going back. Needs `support.read`.

schema.description: Required. A value of your own, up to 255 characters; send the same one when you retry.

post.description: Posts in one of the team's chats, as the key; in a channel shared with a supplier, the supplier reads it. Needs `support.write`.

reply_to.description: A message id: an answer in its thread.

available.description: Whether this Insyte can run the website chat at all.

get.description: The stores' website chats: on or off, and how many chats each has. Needs `support.read`.

theme_updated.description: Whether the store's theme loads the chat; a connected chat shows nothing until it does.

sends_at.description: When it leaves; until then a person can still call it off.

mailbox_id.description: The mailbox a mail thread is in; null for a chat.

channel_id.description: The chat channel a chat came in on; null for mail.

store_id.description: The store a chat came in at; mail is no store's.

preview.description: The start of the last message.

agent_state.description: A chat's: Insyte's customer agent handled it, handed it over to the team (or a person took it over), or holds it.

taken_over_by.description: The member who took a chat over.

order_number.description: A chat's customer's latest order in its store.

messages.description: A mail thread's messages, oldest first.

chat.description: A website chat's messages, oldest first.

send_state.description: scheduled while its undo window lasts: the shopper does not see it yet.

sent_by.description: Who of the team sent it.

send_state.description: What went out: scheduled while its undo window lasts.

mailbox_id.description: The mailbox a mail thread is in; null for a chat.

channel_id.description: The chat channel a chat came in on; null for mail.

store_id.description: The store a chat came in at; mail is no store's.

preview.description: The start of the last message.

agent_state.description: A chat's: Insyte's customer agent handled it, handed it over to the team (or a person took it over), or holds it.

taken_over_by.description: The member who took a chat over.

order_number.description: A chat's customer's latest order in its store.

failure.description: Why an answer did not come: budget, model, rate, interrupted; limit when it settled with what it had.

text.description: The question, or the answer's words with its figures and records in place.

withheld.description: The answer read from a store this key no longer reaches, and is not given back.

kind.description: order, ticket, chargeback, customer, supplier, store or return.

path.description: The console page that opens it.

label.description: What the number is, in Dutch: Vertraagde bestellingen.

path.description: The console page that holds its rows.

source.description: What it was written from: `orders`, or `import` (an imported file).

source_id.description: The import's id, for an export of one.

failure.description: Why a `failed` export failed: `too_many_rows` when it would hold more than 1,000,000 rows.

expires_at.description: When the file is removed: seven days after it was written.

header.description: The file's first row, the column names.

state.description: `done` once a member imported it; `parsed` while it waits for that; `failed` when it could not be read.

error.description: Why it could not be read: not text, no rows, over 50,000 rows, a row over 100 columns, a cell over 32,767 characters, a quote that never closes, or the read gave up.

state.description: warning: Insyte is handling an incident; broken: the store needs the operator (connect it again).

incidents.description: Open ones first, then those resolved in the last seven days (five at most).

kind.description: webhook_gap: no order webhook for two hours while Shopify still changes orders; token_expiring: the grant lapses within seven days; token_expired: Shopify refused a new token; scope_missing: a grant the sync needs is missing; rate_limited: Shopify's request bucket ran nearly empty; sync_failed: the import gave up, or two sweeps in a row failed.

summary.description: What is wrong, in Dutch, as the console says it.

anyOf.description: The lowest share of the bucket left, 0 to 1.

text.description: The step in Dutch, as the console says it.

tried.description: What Insyte already did about it, oldest first.

revenue_minor.description: Counted revenue (paid, not cancelled or refunded).

roas.description: revenue / ad spend, 0 without ad spend.

currency.description: The workspace's currency, every amount's (minor units).

rate.description: percent: the share of revenue, 0 to 100.

rate_minor.description: per_order: the amount per counted order.

reads_from_source.description: An ad line whose account is connected: its untyped months are what the account reports.

closed.description: The month ended and was closed; a running month has no payouts.

to_approve.description: Ended months' payouts past their return window, not approved yet.

code.description: The affiliate's discount code at the store.

rate.description: Commission in percent of an order's subtotal.

earned.description: Commission to date, reversals taken off, pending included.

discount.description: Whether the code exists as a Shopify discount: made, pending (being made), failed or off (no store).

from_provider.description: The case came in through a payment connection; false for one opened by hand in Insyte.

reason.description: item_not_received, not_as_described, unauthorized, duplicate or other.

reason_code.description: The reason as the provider or the team named it.

deadline_at.description: When the evidence must be in at the provider.

won_pct.description: Won out of decided, in whole percent.

from_provider.description: The case came in through a payment connection; false for one opened by hand in Insyte.

reason.description: item_not_received, not_as_described, unauthorized, duplicate or other.

reason_code.description: The reason as the provider or the team named it.

deadline_at.description: When the evidence must be in at the provider.

state.description: `filed`: what it sends leaves once the undo window has passed. `execution_failed`: it did not go (see `execution_error`); filing it again tries again.

action.description: What filing runs, as the key's own call would: approving the return or the check, mailing the shopper of a delayed order the words in `after`, opening a reorder ticket for a sold-out product, or gathering a chargeback's evidence pack. `reconnect_store` needs a person at Shopify's approval page and cannot be filed with a key. A plate an agent asked for (its autonomy is Eerst vragen) carries the tool it called, by that tool's name.

dimension.description: How long is left, in words (Dutch).

confidence.description: 0–1, computed by the rule from the records.

proposal.description: The plate Insyte drew for the row, while it is open; file it with `POST /proposals/{id}/file`.

conversations.description: Website chats the agent heard today, in the key's stores.

handled.description: Of those, answered by the agent and not handed over.

waiting.description: Handed over and not taken by a person yet, as far as the agent saw.

first_reply_seconds.description: The agent's first reply, on average.
